The most plausible classes are a boron-preserving borylative cross-coupling or a conjunctive/1,2-metallate rearrangement-derived coupling; Zweifel olefination is less likely unless an alkenyl boronate and a demonstrable boron-to-alkene rearrangement are present.

Plausible, but not database-confirmed, reagent families are Pd(0)/Pd(II) or Ni(0)/Ni(II) catalysts with a base such as K2CO3, Cs2CO3, KOtBu, or NaOH in dioxane/water, THF/water, toluene, or DMF/NMP; boron-preserving variants may require a diboron reagent or a boryl-metal reagent and, depending on mechanism, an oxidant (for oxidative coupling) or reductant (for Ni/Pd turnover). Exact selection cannot be assigned without the actual reaction SMILES and boron motif.
